name: A New Heart

provenance.detail: Josh opens Glory on the Move as a six-week series in Ezekiel whose goal is to remind the church of the unseen, and later names the series aim as God changing hearts for his glory. In Can These Bones Live he reads Ezekiel 36 on a new heart and a heart of flesh.
Jeremy named the gold Ezekiel block A New Heart: Glory on the Move through From Exile to Emmanuel.

description: Six weeks in Ezekiel: glory on the move, a watchman’s diet, unseen worship, failed shepherds, dry bones, and a river from the temple.
note: Josh frames six weeks through Ezekiel’s visions. The series name is not printed on the gold artwork. Week six lands on new hearts, a new shepherd, a new covenant, and new temples as glory comes home.

provenance.detail: Josh names a six-week series in Ezekiel and reads the opening vision of glory.
Jeremy placed Glory on the Move as week one of A New Heart.
Josh says last week they approached the throne and this series is about God changing hearts, then exposits the watchman and the scroll.
Jeremy included The Watchman’s Diet in A New Heart.
Josh reads Ezekiel 8 fourteen months after chapter 1 and traces hidden idolatry in the temple.
Jeremy included The Unseen Church in A New Heart.
Josh takes Ezekiel 33 and 34 on watchmen and shepherds, recalling the week-two watchman call.
Jeremy included From Neglect to Rescue in A New Heart.
Josh recaps the series journeys and reads the valley of dry bones, including Ezekiel 36 on a new heart.
Jeremy included Can These Bones Live? in A New Heart.
Josh closes the Ezekiel series from chapters 40 through 48 as glory returns and the river flows, naming new hearts among the series gifts.
Jeremy named From Exile to Emmanuel as Ezekiel, A New Heart.
